why: v1.4's target mixes whether a withdrawal happened with when. Ranking on approval age alone reaches 98% of its average precision and reproduces its headline lead times exactly, so the binary formulation could not separate timing from merit. v2 changes the unit of analysis, not the data.
unit: one EU-approved substance in one year at risk
outcome: EU non-renewal inside a horizon starting that year
evaluation: folds grouped by substance; forward splits reported separately

limits.linear_model_recovers: about a fifth of the boosted-tree gain

tables.survival_h1.csv: arms, per-group contributions and forward splits at a one-year horizon
tables.survival_h3.csv: the same at three years, the horizon the watchlist uses
tables.v2_survival_retest.csv: node embeddings re-tested on the panel, where they lose by more
